label: Maternal mortality ratio
reliability_criteria: Canonical tier = UN DYB Table 17 maternal deaths (provided to the UNSD via WHO cause-of-death statistics) and the ratios the UN Statistics Division computes from them per 100,000 live births, 13 editions 2001-2022 (2015 recovered v10, wired v12), C/U/|/+ quality-coded as printed. Medium, not high: maternal deaths are the classic under-reported cause even inside otherwise-complete civil registration (obstetric deaths misclassified to disease chapters), and the collector's own editorial rule refuses to compute ratios where the data is judged incomplete — the series' honest limits are part of the signal. Witness tier = UN MMEIG modeled estimates through two doors (OWID: the 2020 round, 200 entities, 1751-2020; World Bank: the 2023 round, annual 1985-2023), which exist precisely where registration cannot serve.
license: Mixed, per source (see "sources"): UN DYB = UN data reuse policy (attribution required, no endorsement implied); OWID witness = CC-BY-4.0 (content: UN MMEIG estimates); World Bank witness = CC-BY-4.0 (content: UN MMEIG estimates).
notes:
THE FOURTH INDICATOR, THE PUREST COLLECTOR DEGRADATION CASE (P3b): DYB Table 17 prints, per country-year, a "Number" row (registered maternal deaths, WHO-collected cause-of-death statistics) and — only where the collector judges the data reliable enough — a "Rate" row. That editorial rule is the indicator's own built-in honesty, and it lands at two depths: a Rate row with "..." in a given year (counts published, no ratio computed for that year — v9 merge semantics keep those as value=null points carrying the printed quality code), and a country with a Number-ONLY block and no Rate row at all (Libya in the 2024 edition: 12 deaths in 2016, no ratio published) — the latter leaves no point in the ratio indicator; since v12 the counts block has its own indicator (maternal_deaths), the wiring this note deferred for three versions.
THE RATIO IS THE COLLECTOR'S PUBLISHED FIGURE, NOT OURS: the rates are computed by the UN Statistics Division from the country counts and Table 9 live births (printed Notes17), not by the countries themselves. We republish the collector's published ratio as-is — the as-reported discipline applies to the collector's publication, it does not make us re-derive anything. Unit: maternal deaths per 100,000 live births in the same year.
THE 13-EDITION LOOP (v12): 2011-2015 + 2017-2024 — the 2015 edition, recovered in v10 through the legacy /dyb2015/Table17.xls pattern (its own per-table links are dead), is wired here at priority 9: its 2005-2014 window adds keys the later editions dropped and re-arbitrates the 2014-and-older vintages (verified live 2026-09-13: the file parses clean, 77 rate-printing countries / 509 valued ratios, 0 unresolved entity names). Edition 2016 stays deliberately absent (FILEPASS-encrypted, zero coverage loss — its window is covered by 2014 + 2015 + 2017).
TWO TABLE-17-SPECIFIC AS-REPORTED ANNOTATIONS: the "diamond" marker on ratio cells = "Ratios based on 30 or fewer maternal deaths" (small_base, e.g. France 2019 and every Mauritius/Italy ratio — a small-numbers caveat the front should render, not hide); per-year footnote refs that for this table often RESTATE the quality code (the Footnotes sheet's notes 1-4 are literally "The code is C/+C/U/+U") and sometimes carry country-specific caveats — Russia's note 5 in the 2011/2014 editions documents that 2001-2003 data exclude the Chechnya region.
PRE-1975 CAVEAT (outside our window, documented for completeness): in issues prior to 1975 the DYB calculated maternal mortality against the female population, not live births — those rates are not comparable. Our wired window (2001-2022 via editions 2011-2015 + 2017-2024) is entirely on the modern definition. The ICD-10-bold convention (bold = ICD-10 classified) is a TYPEFACE signal, not a cell value: like Table 15's italics it is not carried — the C/U/| code column is its machine-readable equivalent.
WITNESS TIER, TWO DOORS OF ONE ROOT (un_mmeig — and two ROUNDS of it): owid `maternal-mortality` — the UN MMEIG modeled estimates, 200 entities 1751-2020 (the 2020 round), multi-variable CSV (field pinned to "Maternal mortality ratio"). worldbank SH.STA.MMRT — the same modeling family's 2023 round, annual 1985-2023, integer print. The doors diverge on overlapping years BECAUSE the model was revised between rounds (verified live: South Sudan 1987 = 6774.7 OWID vs 8045 WB; Egypt 2020 = 16.8 OWID vs 31 WB) — the divergence view displays the revision, the root field explains why they still agree in structure. The canonical/witness spread is structural too: e.g. Egypt canonical (as registered) ~12-33 vs witness (modeled) ~50-70 in overlapping years — the collector only hears what the registration system catches.
THE WITNESS GRID (WDI's own print): SH.STA.MMRT arrives as WDI's full 1960-2025 year grid; the series itself is valued 1985-2023 (annual, ~194 entities every year). The year slots outside the series' window (1960-1984, 2024-2025) ride as explicit null gap points — the same null discipline as the trailing-2025 slots on the IGME codes, readable as "the provider prints no estimate for this slot", never silently dropped. The entities with no MMEIG estimate at all (23 of WDI's 217 country-classified entities) stay as all-gap witness series.
